subject.title: fix(codex): keep native QA sandboxing out of production

question: Does the Codex owner confirm that the QA launcher’s final temporary-root overrides and the matching turn sandbox policy are the intended upstream Codex contract for both live and mock QA runs?
rationale: This is a security-sensitive ownership boundary between production configuration and an isolated native QA harness, and repository policy requires direct upstream Codex source verification before a Codex verdict.

options.title: Confirm upstream sandbox contract
options.body: Verify the native Codex argument-precedence and turn-policy behavior directly, then merge if it matches the tested QA containment model.

options.title: Keep the existing production-only behavior
options.body: Decline the QA-owned override path if the upstream contract cannot guarantee consistent launcher and turn confinement.

recommendation.title: Confirm upstream sandbox contract
recommendation.body: Verify the native Codex argument-precedence and turn-policy behavior directly, then merge if it matches the tested QA containment model.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the related merged native Codex QA implementation and authored this ownership correction.
